full_judgment:
3. Mr. M.G. Rabbani the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the claimant petitioners has submitted that the suit lands having formed or re-appeared long before the amendment of the provision of section 86 and 87 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, retrospectivity of these sections cannot go before Part-V of the said Act came into force. According to him section 87 which is in Part-V cannot be brought into operation before the date when Part-V was given effect to, and that Part-V of the Act having come into force on 5-8-1965 in the District of Faridpur the order of abatement of the suit by applying the provisions of P.O. Nos. 135 and 137 of 1972 was clearly misconceived. In support of his submission he has referred to the decision of Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in the cases reported in Vol.1 Bangladesh Supreme Court Report, Page 201 (Abdul Mannan and others V. Kulada Ranjan Mowali and others). Their Lordships of the Appellate Division have held : 

 4. Admittedly the suit lands formed or the accretion took place before passing of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as such the application of the provision of P.O. 135 and 137 of 1972 is clearly misconceived and the learned Subordinate Judge committed an apparent error of law in passing an order of abatement of the suit on the ground that the suit is hit under the provisions of P.O. 135 and 137 of 1972.
